ground_truth_root_cause: The OTel collector's OTLP HTTP exporter targeting the Stripe telemetry endpoint (https://stripe-telemetry.internal:9411) became unreachable shortly after the deploy of cf3ba5c857d1 at 2026-05-13T15:04:07Z, which bumped Gradle production dependencies for both the otel-collector and stripe-telemetry-exporter components. The dependency bump introduced an incompatible change in the stripe-telemetry-exporter's gRPC/HTTP client library, causing the exporter process to crash and making stripe-telemetry.internal:9411 refuse connections. With the OTel pipeline stalled, the payment-service's Stripe webhook processor lost its telemetry-backed acknowledgement path, causing webhook round-trips to time out at 10s. This triggered the circuit breaker (OPEN at 15:16:08Z), which caused Stripe to re-deliver unacknowledged webhooks, generating a retry storm of 847 duplicate charge attempts within 60 seconds.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back the stripe-telemetry-exporter and otel-collector to the pre-cf3ba5c857d1 Gradle dependency versions to restore the OTLP exporter and bring stripe-telemetry.internal:9411 back online. 2. Once the OTel pipeline recovers, reset the circuit breaker in payment-service to allow webhook processing to resume. 3. Drain the webhook retry queue by temporarily increasing worker concurrency and enabling Stripe's idempotency-key deduplication to prevent duplicate charges. 4. Audit the postgres connection pool exhaustion and release held connections before re-enabling full webhook ingestion. Total estimated remediation time: 45–90 minutes.
